continuity_scope: The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom original Nintendo Switch release, English-language Nintendo official product/character-portal boundary (12 May 2023). The game is recorded as a sequel to Breath of the Wild, but Breath of the Wild remains a separate game continuity; no broader series timeline, earlier Link/Zelda/Ganon incarnation, Switch 2 Edition, upgrade feature, adaptation, or unreviewed patch is merged into character claims.

Nintendo Zelda Portal: Characters, Tears of the Kingdom Link entry
Nintendo: Get to know Link's four new abilities in The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom
coverage_rule: All stable named individual dramatic characters with a directly claim-level profile in the selected official Tears of the Kingdom witnesses: Link only. Nintendo's character portal identifies this game-specific Link as the hero who defeated the Great Calamity in Breath of the Wild and describes his Upheaval/right-arm crisis role. The selected material does not give an equivalent claim-level individual profile for Zelda, Ganondorf, sages, champions, or other named characters in this exact game scope. No franchise-wide identity is invented from titles or cross-game name reuse.
omissions: All player-controlled ability use, route choices, constructs, weapons, puzzle solutions, saves, game outcomes, and playthrough-specific actions. Link is a stable named character, while player mechanics remain attributes rather than extra nodes.

Zelda, Ganondorf, sages, champions, rulers, allies, enemies, and all other named individuals because the selected official Tears of the Kingdom witnesses lack a matching individual claim-level profile for them.
Peoples/races, roles, sages/champions as categories, items, places, Triforce/magic, timelines, previous games' incarnations, mechanics, and Nintendo Switch system features as character nodes.

Breath of the Wild as a separate character pass; all earlier/later Zelda games and multiple Link/Zelda/Ganon identities; Nintendo Switch 2 Edition and Upgrade Pack features; unreviewed patches; localization variants; fan/community/wiki materials; walkthroughs, guides, videos, data mines, and secondary databases.
uncertainties: The product page and character portal are official high-level references, not a dialogue/codex archive. They support only the stated Link profile and mechanics/premise terms; no complete plot, relationship, or character roster is inferred.

Nintendo describes Tears of the Kingdom as a Breath of the Wild sequel, while its Zelda Portal explicitly treats entries under the same character name across series games as distinct lives/memories. This pass preserves the Tears of the Kingdom record rather than treating series names as one continuous individual.
The product page says players decide their own path and build/play in varied ways; no specific player choice, route, alliance, death, or ending is asserted.

The reviewed original Switch product page lists many supported languages; only English wording is used. Nintendo Switch 2 has a separate edition/upgrade context, so compatibility/performance/save differences and later version behavior remain outside this original-release audit.
No DLC story/character material is documented by the selected sources. The audit makes no claim that no future or regional content exists; it records only its evidence boundary.
evidence_basis: First-party Nintendo product, character-portal, and official news pages only. No fan wiki, Wikipedia, community guide, walkthrough, chronology/timeline chart, lore video, data mine, or secondary database is used as canonical evidence.
